$comment: Shot list entry (sand-y0u.6): the manifest is ahead of the binary. The image has NOT been fetched yet — run the download in docs/imagery-phase-1.md, then `npm run media`. Provenance verified against the archive record on 2026-08-24.

original.description: German troops marching in formation past a public garden in a town. The Nationaal Archief record carries no caption of its own and describes it as "Duitse troepen lopen in formatie langs een plantsoen in een stad (België?)" — the question mark is the archive’s: Belgium is the catalogue’s inference, not an established fact.
original.photographer: not identified in the record ("Unknown author")
original.archive: Nationaal Archief (Netherlands), inventory reference Bestanddeelnr 22005 026, via Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: CC0 1.0 (Commons record: LicenseShortName "CC0"; UsageTerms "Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication"). Nationaal Archief releases this collection into the public domain.

colorization.status: not colorized. Recommendation: colorize — feldgrau M1910 with red piping and the covered Pickelhaube are documented, and the pack has no photograph of a German column on the march in Belgium.

content_policy: ok — troops marching in a street, no gore
caption: A German column marching through a town in 1914. The catalogue places it in Belgium with a question mark, and so does this caption: what is certain is the formation, the field-grey and the year.
credit: Original photograph: photographer not identified, 1914; Nationaal Archief, Bestanddeelnr 22005 026; CC0 / public domain.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API. The archive’s own uncertainty about the country is carried through into the caption rather than tidied away — the town is not identified and must not be named. Fills the bead’s "German columns in Belgium" slot as well as any verified record allows.
